title.narrative: The Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy, and Accountability (YW4A) Programme

description.narrative: Influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of 18 laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Palestine by 2025.

The programme aims to strengthen and diversify young women’s participation and amplify their voices to effectively influence decision-making towards gender-just laws, policies, norms, and practices related to their bodily integrity and equal participation.

description.narrative: Under intermediate outcome (IO) 4, also referred to as Pathway 4, the Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy and Accountability (YW4A) programme aims to influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Palestine by 2025.

title.narrative: WRGE 1.1. (WRG001) # of (targeted) laws, policies and strategies adopted, amended, withdrawn, better used or implemented to eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls in public and private life.

description.narrative: Draft law on domestic violence improved and lobbying with the government to pass it into law.Lobbying government to remove exception clause or at least specify the reasons for the exception in 2019 child marriage law.

comment.narrative: There is a need to:- Amend the draft Palestinian Penal Code in line with the CRC, CEDAW, General Recommendation No. 19 and other relevant recommendations and charters, and endeavoring to approve it as soon as possible.- Define and codify gender-based violence in the applicable laws in Palestine.- Include marital rape in the forms of domestic violence that should be punished- Protect service providers for victims and survivors of domestic violence.- Activate the mandatory reporting of cases of violence against women and girls and setting up effective systems to protect whistle-blowers.Amend the draft law to protect the family from violence and speeding up its approval.- Put restrictions on protection orders contained in the draft law on Family Protection from Violence and differentiating between them along the lines of what is stated in the Model Legislation for Protection from Domestic Violence.
Draft law on domestic violence improved and lobbying with government to pass it into law.

An amended version of the draft law was developed and submitted to the cabinet for debate in 2021 but there has been no further progress at official level. During virtual sessions with NGOs and government to learn from the experiences of women activists in other countries, which were implemented as part of the programme in early 2022, the Minister for Women's Affairs indicated that she was in favor of passing the law, but some ministers were opposed to its enactment. Since then opposition has hardened, notwithstanding lobbying and awareness raising activities conducted through YW4A with increasing intensity and participation by young women (see section 5.1.2). In meetings with the ministers for justice, women’s affairs, and social development in the first quarter of 2025, all three indicated that passage of the law is unlikely at this time, the first two putting the blame on the increasing movement against the endorsement of the Bill from conservative religious groups, which is making the government reluctant to pass it. The Minister for Social Development observed that their priorities and mandates are shifting to offering relief support through the emergency committees in the West Bank and Gaza, and legal reform is not on their top priorities. On a more positive note, the ministers for justice and women’s affairs noted that their legal teams are currently working together on the amendment of the Personnel Status Law, and will include articles addressing women’s protection in the amended law. Unfortunately, analysis by Equality Now indicates that the draft still allows the legal exception for child marriage and is affected by several other gender discriminatory clauses.
no changes

There are not changes in regards to the enactment of the domestic violence bill and removing the legal exception to child marriage. However, several awareness campaigns at community levels targeting the social norms that perpetuate CM were implemented.

Draft law on domestic violence improved and lobbying with government to pass it into law.Preparing draft law on sexual harassment in public spaces.Lobbying government to remove exception clause or at least specify the reasons for the exception in 2019 child marriage law.

WROs in Palestine have joined a national coalition (El Muntada) advocating for the domestic violence bill. The complex legal framework and absence of a Legislative assembly in Palestine present an additional complexity to law reform.

title.narrative: WRGE 1.1 (WRG001 # of laws, policies andnorms, implemented forsustainable and inclusivedevelopment.

comment.narrative: There is the need to clearly define what sexual harassment is in the draft penal code, and imposing penalties on its various forms.

Promoting development and implementation of regulations on sexual harassment in public spaces under the Palestinian Labour Law. Lobbying government to remove exception clause or at least specify the reasons for the exception in 2019 child marriage law (and enforce deterrent penalties).

During 2023, YWCA tried to join a newly formed national coalition which had drafted a new labor law that included articles relating to workplace sexual harassment. Unfortunately, YWCA was not able to join the coalition but progress continued on the draft law.Towards the end of 2024, through discussions with the Ministry of Labour, it became clear that there was greater political will to address workplace harassment, and discussions on amending labor laws to include more explicit safeguards. In a subsequent meeting with the Ministry in January 2025, ministry representatives acknowledged the social and legal challenges to receiving complaints, especially by female workers, and a technical committee comprised of WROs, YW, Ministry of Labour and the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions (PGFTU) was established. That committee had its first meeting in March and, through another four meetings from April to June, has developed drafts of two important new official instruments: the new draft labour bill mentioned above, which now includes recognition and criminalisation of workplace sexual harassment; and an administrative decree that would provide directives and guidelines for the development of workplace sexual harassment policiesProgress at government level has been very slow but in conversations with programme partners during the first quarter of 2025, the Ministers of Justice and Women Affairs made promises on producing an amended Personal Status Law including amendments to the article stipulating the exceptions of child marriage and making amendments to the age of marriage. During Q3, they shared the amended version for consultation with Palestinian WROs, and held meetings to listen to their feedbacks and comments. Young women from YW4A took part in those meetings and the revision of the draft amended law. Details on the outcomes of those meetings will be shared by YWCA Palestine and added to this report in October 2025.There has been positive change in relation to religious laws on marriage. The ELCJHL (Evangelical Lutheran Church in Jordan and the Holy Land - a partner under Pathway 3) changed its law on Personnel Status in 2015, and the continuous efforts (policy mapping, conferences, meetings with decision makers and government officials) inspired the biggest church in Palestine, the Greek Orthodox Church in 2023 to change its laws raising marriage age to 18.
no changes

The initial strategy for 2023 was to engage in legal advocacy toward the ratification of ILO C190; however, following the outbreak of was in Palestine in Q4, the WROs and YW are focused on partnering with trade unions and other stakeholders to promote better protections for women in the workplace.
Lobbying government and concerned administrations not to apply exception clause from 2019 child marriage law

WROs are working with young girls, marriage registrars, and religious leaders to influence and shape social norms that ultimately will lead/cause pressure to remove the exception to the legal minimum age for marriage.

description.narrative: Under intermediate outcome (IO) 4, also referred to as Pathway 4, the Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy and Accountability (YW4A) programme aims to influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation in Palestine by 2025

title.narrative: WRGE 2.1 (WRG016) # of laws, policies andnorms, implemented forsustainable and inclusivedevelopment.

description.narrative: Better implementation of national laws on local elections to ensure the inclusion of women and youth.

comment.narrative: In order to increase this participation, the following measures/actions can be taken:- Conducting studies, including comparative studies, in order to assess the full reasons that explain the very low political participation of women and their needs.- Introduce effective measures (legal and administrative) in order to promote equality and counter existing stereotyes in a culture that consecrates discrimination- Empower women socially, politically, and legally to improve her political participation- Increase the existing quota in local council elections to 30%Election law for local councils should include a provision allowing women to occupy the position of vice-president in case a male candidate wins the presidency, and vice versa- At the level of unions, the quota should be introduced to guarantee the election of women to their councils.
4b) Better implementation of national laws on local elections for inclusion of women and youth

2023 was not an election year in Palestine, and the WROs and young women focused their advocacy on increasing the political participation of young women in relation to student councils in universities and demonstrating their leadership potential to their peers to promote increased participation.
Increasing young women's political participation through inclusion in university student council elections.

A survey on participation in student councils and university politics was sent to approximately 1,000 young women participating in YW4A and received 301 responses between December 2024 and January 2025. We do not have baseline data with which to compare the responses but they showed an encouraging level of participation and interest. 14% of respondents indicated that they are members of student councils while 31% said that they are involved in university / student politics in some other way. Their aspirations regarding future participation are even more encouraging with 27% saying they would like to be candidates in the next student council elections and 70% being willing to engage in activities at their university to promote YW’s political participation.We have not been able to obtain statistics to understand whether there has been increased female participation in student councils over the programme period. Statistics from the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics indicated 12% of council members were young women in 2019 but we have not yet obtained the numbers from the last elections, which were held in 2023.

Encouraging young women to run at the level of local councils and increase their participation according to the existing 25% quotaBetter implementation of national laws on local elections, encouraging young women's political participation, and ensuring the inclusion of women and youth in political processes.

Palestine last had national elections in 1994. WROs are working on ensuring young women increase their participation in the elections of local councils, student unions, and where possible professional unions/associations.
